correctness.rationale: For almost all Voronoi cell points, the first site is the origin and the second squared-distance excess is the minimum of finite affine lattice-vector slacks; the endpoint is the shortest squared norm. The midpoint decomposition makes non-relevant constraints redundant for every nonnegative threshold. Orthogonal decomposition along the shortest-vector span yields bounded nondegenerate polytopes K and H and a Jacobian epsilon^r, giving the exact strictly positive leading coefficient. Finite affine-parametric halfspaces have stable combinatorics near the endpoint, hence an exact polynomial of degree at most d and the O(epsilon^(r+1)) remainder. The self-contained exact-rational checker was executed successfully for nonorthogonal planar examples and orthogonal 3D cases. The finite cases corroborate, but do not prove, the all-dimensional theorem.

evidence: Koçak–Ratiu arXiv:1008.2040v1 establishes piecewise polynomial Euclidean inner parallel volume for arbitrary polytopes, and a rectangle example with variable vanishing order at inradius.
McKilliam et al. arXiv:1405.7014v1 establish the relevant-vector Voronoi representation.

The present inward motion uses an identical *squared-distance* decrement of the lattice-vector thresholds, equivalently Euclidean facet-speed inversely proportional to vector norm, unlike ordinary Euclidean erosion.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General polytope polynomiality is covered and is not itself presented as novel. Existing fixed-Euclidean-speed erosion laws and Voronoi representations do not determine the all-lattice exponent r or the specific product of intrinsic volumes on complementary shortest-vector subspaces.

originality.rationale: Original contribution is the exact upper-tail exponent equal to the shortest-vector span rank and its mixed-dimensional positive coefficient for every full-rank Euclidean lattice. Standard Voronoi halfspaces, well-roundedness, and piecewise polynomial inner-tube volumes are acknowledged as prior knowledge, not novelty. Primary sections and a highly relevant published lattice-clearance result were materially compared; no inspected theorem gives or implies the all-lattice probabilistic rank-recovery statement. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Priority in obscure lattice decoding or reliability-margin literature cannot be excluded solely by semantic searches.
General results on anisotropic parametric-polytope erosion may contain a structurally equivalent rank-of-collapse statement not indexed by the searched terminology.
The BCC/FCC clearance result gives certain special cases after facet-normal rescaling; no novelty is asserted for them.

value.rationale: The exponent of one geometrically natural, randomly sampled quantizer decision statistic determines the rank of the shortest-vector span and therefore whether the lattice is well-rounded. The theorem is uniform over all dimensions and includes a concrete mixed-dimensional volume coefficient and an exact endpoint polynomial. Its nonorthogonal planar examples show genuinely different tail orders despite identical minimum vector squared length. The objective is a structural identification law, not an arbitrary parameter recomputation or a restatement of generic polytope polynomiality.
